'''Binte biluhuta''' is a poured boiled-[[sweet corn]] or [[corn soup]] originates from the [[Gorontalese cuisine]], [[Sulawesi|Sulawesi island]], [[Indonesia]].<ref>Ichsan, T.N., 2021. Binte Biluhuta: Tradition, Culinary Techniques and Nutritional Value. ''International Journal of Advanced Food and Gastronomy'', ''1''(2).</ref>

Binte biluhuta is a typical food of [[Gorontalo people|Gorontalese]], which is referred to [[Gorontalo people]]. Binte biluhuta is also known as '''''Milu Siram''''' in Gorontalo Malay language.<ref>Kadir, S. and Kes, M., 2022. ''Kuliner Bergizi Berbasis Budaya''. Absolute Media.</ref> 

Binte biluhuta is served hot with [[Coconut|shredded coconut]], [[Basil|basil leaves]], [[Skipjack tuna|shredded skipjack tuna]], and [[shrimp]].
